title: Regularisation: L1 and L2, dropout, data augmentation and hyperparameter search
summary: L1/L2 and proximal reasoning, weight-decay distinctions, exact/Monte Carlo dropout and task-valid augmentation studies.

objectives.description: Derive L1/L2 solutions and distinguish nonsmooth thresholding from gradient shrinkage.
Explain when L2 penalties and weight decay agree or differ.
Calculate dropout expectations and limits under a specified mask convention.
Design label-valid augmentation and validation-based regularisation studies.

preparation.description: Read L1/L2, dropout, augmentation and hyperparameter selection; record penalty coefficient and mask conventions.

activities.title: Lecture notes and primary reading
activities.instructions: Work through the notes with the assigned source open. Reproduce each worked calculation or derivation on paper, including its assumptions, before reading the next step. Write one question that remains unresolved.

activities.title: Problem sheet: calculation, explanation and transfer
activities.instructions: Attempt the problems independently first. Use one hint at a time if useful, and record which help you used. Show the reasoning that connects the model and its assumptions to each answer; compare the reference only after a substantial attempt.

activities.title: Return without the notes
activities.instructions: On a later study day, close the notes and reconstruct the core relation and its assumptions, then explain the failure case from the last problem. Compare with your saved work and correct one gap. This practice does not itself certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to judge the objectives: explain assumptions, complete the independent calculations and justify the final transfer/synthesis. The final exercise is the recorded checkpoint; its acceptance alone is not a claim that all course outcomes are mastered.

commonMisconceptions.claim: L2 regularisation and weight decay are identical for every optimiser.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Their equivalence depends on the update rule; adaptive/preconditioned scaling can separate them.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Mean-preserving dropout preserves every downstream output and loss.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Nonlinear operations do not generally commute with expectation.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Augmentation creates independent samples with automatically valid labels.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Descendants share their source, and label invariance/equivariance must be checked for the task.
